passages.english: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James, To those who are called, loved by God the Father, and kept in Jesus Christ: Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

lines.text: Jude is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Jude is also a brother of James.
Jude writes to those whom God has called.
God the Father loves those called by God.
And they are kept safe in Jesus Christ.
May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

passages.english: Beloved, although I made every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I felt it necessary to write and urge you to contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints.

lines.text: Beloved, Jude longed to write to you about the salvation we share.
But Jude felt he must write to you for another reason.
Jude urges you to contend earnestly for the faith — to fight to defend the true message about Jesus.
God entrusted this faith once for all to the saints — His holy people.

passages.english: For certain men have crept in among you unnoticed—ungodly ones who were designated long ago for condemnation. They turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality, and they deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.

lines.text: Some men have been ungodly.
These men have secretly crept in among you — some people have gathered with Christians while hiding their ungodliness.
Long ago, God marked these men out for condemnation — God will judge these ungodly people.
They twist the grace of our God into a license for immoral living — for example, by teaching it is okay to sin because God will just forgive you.
And they deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ — eventually their sin leads them to deny Christ.

passages.english: Although you are fully aware of this, I want to remind you that after Jesus had delivered His people out of the land of Egypt, He destroyed those who did not believe.

lines.text: Jesus once saved His people out of the land of Egypt.
But later Jesus destroyed those who did not believe.
You already know this.
Jude wants to remind you that Jesus saved a people, but then judged them for unbelief.

passages.english: And the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling—these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.

lines.text: And some angels did not stay in their own place of authority.
Instead, these angels abandoned their proper home in heaven.
So God has kept these angels in eternal chains, under darkness.
These angels are bound for judgment on that great day.

passages.english: In like manner, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, who indulged in sexual immorality and pursued strange flesh, are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.

lines.text: In the same way as those angels, Sodom, Gomorrah, and the cities around them also sinned.
These cities indulged in sexual immorality.
Sodom, Gomorrah, and the cities around them also pursued strange, unnatural desires.
So God made these cities an example for everyone to see.
These cities suffer the punishment of eternal fire.

passages.english: Yet in the same way these dreamers defile their bodies, reject authority, and slander glorious beings.

lines.text: Yet in the same way, these dreamers also sin — they follow their own false visions.
These dreamers defile their own bodies — for example, through sexual sin, which sins against one's own body.
These dreamers reject authority — refusing to submit to God's rightful authority over them.
And these dreamers slander glorious beings — speaking about angels with arrogant disrespect.

passages.english: But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you!”

lines.text: Michael is a mighty archangel.
Michael once argued with the devil himself.
Michael and the devil argued over the body of Moses.
But even Michael did not dare to bring a slanderous charge against the devil.
Instead, Michael said to the devil, "The Lord rebuke you!"

passages.english: These men, however, slander what they do not understand, and like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.

lines.text: But these men slander what they do not understand — they revile things that are beyond them.
These men are like irrational animals — creatures that cannot reason as a human can.
And the very things these men do by instinct will destroy them — acting on raw natural urges, without thought or reason.

passages.english: Woe to them! They have traveled the path of Cain; they have rushed headlong into the error of Balaam; they have perished in Korah’s rebellion.

lines.text: Woe to these men!
They have traveled the path of Cain — who killed his own brother out of jealousy.
They have rushed into the error of Balaam — who loved money and taught a king to lure God's people into sin.
They have perished in Korah's rebellion — Korah led his followers to defy God's chosen leaders, and all of them were destroyed.

passages.english: These men are hidden reefs in your love feasts, shamelessly feasting with you but shepherding only themselves. They are clouds without water, carried along by the wind; fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted.

lines.text: These men are like hidden reefs — they lie just beneath the surface, and a passing ship is wrecked on them.
They hide among your love feasts — a love feast is a shared meal where your church eats together in fellowship.
They feast with you shamelessly, without the slightest fear.
A shepherd is meant to feed the flock — but these men feed only themselves.
They are like clouds without rain — they promise refreshment but give none, driven along by the wind.
They are like fruitless trees in autumn — autumn is the season for fruit, yet they have none.
They are twice dead — they bear no fruit, and then they are torn out by the roots.

passages.english: They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom blackest darkness has been reserved forever.

lines.text: These men are like wild waves of the sea.
These men foam up their own shame — like a churning sea that tosses up filth, they put their disgrace on open display.
These men are like wandering stars — stars that stray from their path, so no traveler can safely follow them.
God has reserved the blackest darkness for these men forever.

passages.english: Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them: “Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones to execute judgment on everyone, and to convict all the ungodly of every ungodly act of wickedness and every harsh word spoken against Him by ungodly sinners.”

lines.text: Enoch, of the seventh generation from Adam, also prophesied about these men:
Look! The Lord is coming.
He comes with countless thousands of His holy ones.
The Lord comes to judge everyone.
He will prove the guilt of all the ungodly.
The Lord will judge every ungodly act of wickedness they have done.
And the Lord will judge every harsh word that ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.

passages.english: These men are discontented grumblers, following after their own lusts; their mouths spew arrogance; they flatter others for their own advantage.

lines.text: These men are grumblers, never satisfied with anything.
They follow their own sinful desires.
These men use their mouths to speak proud, boastful words.
They flatter others to gain an advantage for themselves.

passages.english: These are the ones who cause divisions, who are worldly and devoid of the Spirit.

lines.text: These men cause divisions, splitting believers apart.
They are worldly — they live by their natural desires.
And they do not have the Holy Spirit.

passages.english: But you, beloved, remember what was foretold by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ when they said to you, “In the last times there will be scoffers who will follow after their own ungodly desires.”

lines.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ sent out apostles.
These apostles foretold what would happen.
So, beloved, remember what they said:
In the last times, scoffers will come — people who mock God and His truth.
These scoffers will follow their own ungodly desires.

passages.english: But you, beloved, by building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you eternal life.

lines.text: But you, beloved — you are dearly loved.
Build yourselves up in your most holy faith.
Pray in the Holy Spirit.
Keep yourselves in the love of God.
Wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ.
His mercy will bring you eternal life.

passages.english: And indeed, have mercy on those who doubt; save others by snatching them from the fire; and to still others show mercy tempered with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.

lines.text: Show mercy to those who doubt — be kind and gentle to those whose faith is weaker.
Save others by snatching them from the fire — they are in great danger, so pull them out quickly.
To still others, show mercy — but with fear, careful not to be pulled into their sin.
Show mercy with fear by hating even the clothing stained by their sin — keep far from all their sin has touched.

passages.english: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy— to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity. Amen.

lines.text: God is able to keep you from stumbling into sin.
One day He will present you before His glory.
God will present you without any fault — perfect and free of all sin.
On that day you will have great joy.
God is the only God.
And God is our Savior.
Now, to Him be glory, majesty, power, and authority.
All this is through Jesus Christ.
Jesus is our Lord.
This glory, majesty, power, and authority is God's before all time, now, and forever.
Amen.
